html:
Lake Titicaca is a large lake high in the Andes on the border of Peru and Bolivia, at about 3,810 metres. It is the largest lake in South America.

Its water softens the frost of the altiplano, so its shores have been among the most farmed parts of the Andes for thousands of years:

  • Early villages of the Chiripa culture, and the Wankarani culture to the south, came first.
  • From about 500 to 1000 the city of Tiwanaku, near the southern shore, ruled a wide sphere, sharing a religious art with the Wari.
  • Then the Aymara kingdoms, such as the Pakajaqi, divided the shores until the Inca took them in the later 1400s.

The Uru fished and lived on floating reed islands. The Incas said their founders came out of the lake. Aymara and Quechua speakers still farm its shores.
sum: Lake Titicaca is a large lake high in the Andes on the border of Peru and Bolivia, at about 3,810 metres. It is the largest lake in South America.
